name: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (120B A12B)
description: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is an open multimodal 120B total / 12B active Mixture-of-Experts model (hybrid Mamba-2 + Attention with a C-RADIO / RADIO vision encoder) built for long-running agents. It accepts text, image, and video inputs and produces text, with up to 1M context, tool use, and configurable reasoning. Released with open weights under OpenMDW-1.1.

license.name: OpenMDW License v1.1
license.description: Open Model, Data and Weights (OpenMDW) License Agreement, version 1.1 - permits commercial and non-commercial use.

benchmarks.name: AA-LCR
benchmarks.description: Agent Arena Long Context Reasoning benchmark
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card; AA-LCR v1.1

benchmarks.name: BrowseComp
benchmarks.description: BrowseComp is a benchmark comprising 1,266 questions that challenge AI agents to persistently navigate the internet in search of hard-to-find, entangled information. The benchmark measures agents' ability to exercise persistence in information gathering, demonstrate creativity in web navigation, and find concise, verifiable answers. Despite the difficulty of the questions, BrowseComp is simple and easy-to-use, as predicted answers are short and easily verifiable against reference answers.
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card

benchmarks.name: CharXiv-R
benchmarks.description: CharXiv-R is the reasoning component of the CharXiv benchmark, focusing on complex reasoning questions that require synthesizing information across visual chart elements. It evaluates multimodal large language models on their ability to understand and reason about scientific charts from arXiv papers through various reasoning tasks.
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card; CharXiv reasoning

benchmarks.name: GDPval-AA
benchmarks.description: GDPval-AA evaluates AI agents on economically valuable professional knowledge-work tasks and reports performance as an Elo score.
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card; GDPval-AA v2 Elo (max_score 3000)
benchmarks.verification_notes: Self-reported from HF 2026-10-15 release card. HF labels GDPval-AA v2; catalog stores absolute Elo under gdpval-aa (not gdpval-aa-2.1).

benchmarks.name: GPQA
benchmarks.description: A challenging dataset of 448 multiple-choice questions written by domain experts in biology, physics, and chemistry. Questions are Google-proof and extremely difficult, with PhD experts reaching 65% accuracy.
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card; GPQA-Diamond
benchmarks.verification_notes: Self-reported from HF 2026-10-15 release card. Catalog has no gpqa-diamond id; sibling Nemotron models store Diamond under gpqa.

benchmarks.name: Humanity's Last Exam
benchmarks.description: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE) is a multi-modal academic benchmark with 2,500 questions across mathematics, humanities, and natural sciences, designed to test LLM capabilities at the frontier of human knowledge with unambiguous, verifiable solutions
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card; HLE text-only

benchmarks.name: IFBench
benchmarks.description: Instruction Following Benchmark evaluating model's ability to follow complex instructions
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card

benchmarks.name: LiveCodeBench v6
benchmarks.description: LiveCodeBench is a holistic and contamination-free evaluation benchmark for large language models for code. It continuously collects new problems from programming contests (LeetCode, AtCoder, CodeForces) and evaluates four different scenarios: code generation, self-repair, code execution, and test output prediction. Problems are annotated with release dates to enable evaluation on unseen problems released after a model's training cutoff.
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card; LiveCodeBench v6

benchmarks.name: MathVision
benchmarks.description: MATH-Vision is a dataset designed to measure multimodal mathematical reasoning capabilities. It focuses on evaluating how well models can solve mathematical problems that require both visual understanding and mathematical reasoning, bridging the gap between visual and mathematical domains.
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card

benchmarks.name: MMLongBench-Doc
benchmarks.description: MMLongBench-Doc evaluates long document understanding capabilities in vision-language models.
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card

benchmarks.name: OCRBench-V2 (en)
benchmarks.description: OCRBench v2 English subset: Enhanced benchmark for evaluating Large Multimodal Models on visual text localization and reasoning with English text content
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card; OCRBench v2 EN

benchmarks.name: OmniScience
benchmarks.description: OmniScience is a broad scientific knowledge and reasoning benchmark that measures both answer accuracy and non-hallucination (calibrated abstention) across science domains.
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card; AA-Omniscience accuracy
benchmarks.verification_notes: Self-reported from HF 2026-10-15 release card. No aa-omniscience id in catalog; sibling Nemotron models store AA-Omniscience accuracy under omniscience.

benchmarks.name: OSWorld-Verified
benchmarks.description: OSWorld-Verified is a verified subset of OSWorld, a scalable real computer environment for multimodal agents supporting task setup, execution-based evaluation, and interactive learning across Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS.
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card

benchmarks.name: SciCode
benchmarks.description: SciCode is a research coding benchmark curated by scientists that challenges language models to code solutions for scientific problems. It contains 338 subproblems decomposed from 80 challenging main problems across 16 natural science sub-fields including mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, and materials science. Problems require knowledge recall, reasoning, and code synthesis skills.
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card; SciCode subtask

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Multilingual
benchmarks.description: A multilingual benchmark for issue resolving in software engineering that covers Java, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Rust, C, and C++. Contains 1,632 high-quality instances carefully annotated from 2,456 candidates by 68 expert annotators, designed to evaluate Large Language Models across diverse software ecosystems beyond Python.
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card

benchmarks.name: SWE-Bench Pro
benchmarks.description: SWE-Bench Pro is an advanced version of SWE-Bench that evaluates language models on complex, real-world software engineering tasks requiring extended reasoning and multi-step problem solving.
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card

benchmarks.name: SWE-Bench Verified
benchmarks.description: A verified subset of 500 software engineering problems from real GitHub issues, validated by human annotators for evaluating language models' ability to resolve real-world coding issues by generating patches for Python codebases.
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card

benchmarks.name: Tau3 Banking
benchmarks.description: τ³-Bench banking domain evaluates agentic models on multi-turn, tool-using customer-support scenarios in a simulated retail banking environment.
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card; τ³-bench (Banking)

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
benchmarks.description: Terminal-Bench 2.1 is an updated release of the Terminal-Bench benchmark that tests AI agents' ability to operate a computer via the terminal. It evaluates how well models handle real-world, end-to-end tasks autonomously, including compiling code, training models, setting up servers, system administration, data science workflows, and security tasks.
benchmarks.analysis_method: NeMo Gym / NeMo Evaluator; BF16 SuperGA as on HF card
